title: Discerning Compatibility and Values
subtitle: Evaluating alignment in the areas that determine marriage success
summary: Chemistry attracts you to someone, but compatibility determines whether you can build a life together. Many couples discover too late that they disagree on fundamental issues: faith, family, finances, life direction. This journey helps you evaluate compatibility in the areas that actually predict marriage success, so you can make wise decisions before commitment.

cover.heroImageDescription: Two puzzle pieces fitting together perfectly, representing compatibility and alignment in values.

targetOutcomes: Understand the difference between chemistry and compatibility
Identify your core values and non-negotiables for marriage
Learn to evaluate compatibility in the areas that matter most
Have productive conversations about difficult topics
Recognize when differences are workable versus fundamental
Make informed decisions about relationship continuation

activities.title: Chemistry Is Not Compatibility
activities.subtitle: Understanding the difference that determines marriage success
activities.whyThisMatters: Chemistry and compatibility are often confused, but they are completely different things. Chemistry is what draws you together; compatibility is what keeps you together. Many relationships with strong chemistry fail because of poor compatibility. Understanding this distinction can save you years of heartache.

frameworkBasis.explanation: Chemistry and compatibility are often confused, but they are completely different things. Chemistry is what draws you together; compatibility is what ...

cards.title: What Chemistry Is
cards.text:
Compatibility is not about how easy the beginning feels.
It is about whether two people can move through pressure, disagreement, and change without losing respect for each other.

If you have ever confused chemistry with alignment, this journey will help you slow down and discern what truly lasts.

Chemistry is the spark, the attraction, the feeling that draws you to someone:

- Physical attraction and desire
- Excitement when you see them
- Easy conversation that flows naturally
- A sense of connection and understanding
- Butterflies, anticipation, longing
- Feeling like you "click"

Chemistry is wonderful. It is also unreliable as a predictor of marriage success.

Chemistry can exist with someone completely wrong for you. It can fade with someone completely right for you. It tells you about attraction, not about whether you can build a life together.

cards.title: What Compatibility Is
cards.text:
Compatibility is alignment in the areas that matter for building a life together:

- Shared core values and beliefs
- Similar life vision and direction
- Aligned views on family, faith, and finances
- Compatible communication and conflict styles
- Mutual respect and admiration
- Shared approach to major life decisions
- Ability to work through disagreements

Compatibility is less exciting than chemistry. It does not give you butterflies.

But it predicts whether you will still be happy in year 20.

The goal is both chemistry AND compatibility.

But if you have to choose, compatibility matters more for long-term happiness.

cards.title: Two Marriages, Two Outcomes
cards.text:
Jake and Melissa had incredible chemistry.

The attraction was instant and intense.

They could not get enough of each other.

Everyone said they were perfect together.

But they never discussed their differences.

Jake wanted kids immediately; Melissa wanted to focus on career.

Jake was a spender; Melissa was a saver.

Jake's faith was casual; Melissa's was central to her life.

Within three years, they were miserable.

The chemistry could not overcome the incompatibility.

Meanwhile, their friends Tom and Rachel had less initial spark.

Their connection grew slowly over time.

But they spent months discussing values, vision, and the things that mattered.

They aligned on faith, family, and finances.

Twenty years later, Tom and Rachel have a thriving marriage.

Jake and Melissa divorced after five.

cards.title: Your Chemistry and Compatibility History
cards.text:
Think about past relationships or interests.

Did you prioritize chemistry or compatibility?

Have you ever had strong chemistry with someone who was clearly incompatible? What happened?

cards.title: You Need Both
cards.text:
The goal is not to ignore chemistry.

Attraction matters in marriage.

The goal is to require BOTH chemistry AND compatibility before committing.

Chemistry without compatibility leads to passionate relationships that implode.

Compatibility without chemistry leads to roommate marriages that feel empty.

You deserve both. Do not settle for one without the other.

This journey will help you evaluate compatibility thoroughly, so that when you find chemistry, you can assess whether it is built on a foundation that will last.

cards.title: A Prayer for Wisdom
cards.text:
Lord, help me see beyond chemistry to compatibility.

Give me wisdom to evaluate what matters for building a life together. Do not let attraction blind me to incompatibility. Do not let fear settle me for compatibility without connection.

Bring me someone with whom I share both spark and substance.

Amen.

activities.title: Identifying Your Core Values
activities.subtitle: Knowing what matters most to you before evaluating others
activities.whyThisMatters: Before you can evaluate compatibility with someone else, you need to know what you value. Many people drift into relationships without clarity about their own priorities, then discover conflicts too late. This activity helps you identify what matters most to you.

frameworkBasis.explanation: Before you can evaluate compatibility with someone else, you need to know what you value. Many people drift into relationships without clarity about t...

cards.title: What Core Values Are
cards.text:
Core values are the fundamental beliefs and priorities that guide your life:

- What you believe is most important
- What you will not compromise on
- What shapes your major decisions
- What you want your life to be about
- What you would sacrifice other things for

Core values are different from preferences.

You might prefer someone who likes hiking, but that is not a core value.

You might require someone who shares your faith, and that IS a core value.

Knowing your core values helps you evaluate compatibility on what actually matters.

cards.title: Values Identification Exercise
cards.text:
Rate the importance of each area (1 = nice to have, 5 = absolutely essential):

• __ Faith and spiritual life
• __ Family and children
• __ Career and ambition
• __ Financial security
• __ Adventure and experiences
• __ Stability and routine
• __ Service and generosity
• __ Health and wellness
• __ Education and growth
• __ Community and friendships
• __ Independence and autonomy
• __ Tradition and heritage

• Your 5s are your core values.

• Your 4s are very important.

• Pay attention to these in evaluating compatibility.

cards.title: Your Non-Negotiables
cards.text:
Based on your values, what are your absolute non-negotiables for a spouse?

What must they share with you? What can you not compromise on no matter how much you like them?

cards.title: Non-Negotiables vs. Preferences
cards.text:
It helps to distinguish:

Non-negotiables (must have or must not have):
- Shared faith commitment
- Agreement on having children
- Freedom from active addiction
- Respect and kindness
- Aligned life direction

Strong preferences (very important but workable):
- Similar education level
- Compatible family backgrounds
- Shared hobbies and interests
- Similar political views

Preferences (nice to have):
- Physical type
- Specific career
- Particular personality style

Be firm on non-negotiables. Be flexible on preferences.

cards.title: A Prayer for Clarity
cards.text:
Lord, show me what I truly value.

Help me distinguish between what is essential and what is preference.

Give me clarity about my non-negotiables so I can evaluate wisely.

Align my values with Yours.

Amen.

activities.title: Faith Compatibility: The Foundation
activities.subtitle: Evaluating spiritual alignment for lifelong partnership
activities.whyThisMatters: For Christians, faith is not one area among many; it is the foundation that shapes everything else. Misalignment here creates tension that affects every other area of life. This activity helps you evaluate spiritual compatibility thoroughly.

frameworkBasis.explanation: For Christians, faith is not one area among many; it is the foundation that shapes everything else. Misalignment here creates tension that affects eve...

cards.title: Why Faith Compatibility Matters Most
cards.text:
Faith shapes everything:

- How you make decisions (seeking God's guidance)
- How you handle conflict (forgiveness, humility)
- How you raise children (spiritual formation)
- How you spend money (generosity, stewardship)
- How you face suffering (hope, trust)
- What your marriage is FOR (reflecting Christ)

If you are not aligned on faith, you are not aligned on the framework for everything else.

Scripture is clear: "Do not be yoked together with unbelievers" (2 Corinthians 6:14). This is not arbitrary restriction; it is wisdom about the difficulty of building a life with someone heading a different direction.

cards.title: What to Evaluate
cards.text:
Faith compatibility involves more than both claiming to be Christian:

Personal faith: Is their relationship with God real and growing? Do they pursue God personally through prayer, Scripture, and obedience?

Church involvement: Are they connected to a faith community? Do they prioritize corporate worship?

Conviction level: How central is faith to their life? Is it foundational or peripheral?

Doctrinal alignment: Do you agree on core beliefs? Are differences on secondary issues workable?

Spiritual leadership: (For women evaluating men) Is he willing and able to lead spiritually?

Faith trajectory: Is their faith growing, stagnant, or declining?

cards.title: Faith Compatibility Questions
cards.text:
Questions to explore together:

- How would you describe your relationship with God right now?
- What does your daily or weekly spiritual life look like?
- What role does church play in your life?
- How does your faith influence major decisions?
- What do you believe about [key doctrinal issues]?
- How would you want to raise children spiritually?
- What does spiritual leadership in marriage look like to you?
- Where do you want to grow spiritually?

Listen not just to answers but to depth, authenticity, and enthusiasm.

cards.title: Your Faith Requirements
cards.text: What level of commitment, involvement, and alignment would you require?

cards.title: A Prayer for Spiritual Unity
cards.text:
Lord, I want a marriage built on shared faith in You.

Help me find someone whose heart is fully Yours, not just someone who knows the right words.

Give me discernment to see authentic faith versus performance.

Bring me a partner I can grow with spiritually for a lifetime.

Amen.

activities.title: Family and Children: Aligned Vision
activities.subtitle: Evaluating compatibility on family life and parenting
activities.whyThisMatters: Disagreement about children and family is one of the most common causes of marriage failure. Do you both want children? How many? How will you raise them? How involved will extended family be? These questions need answers before marriage, not after.

frameworkBasis.explanation: Disagreement about children and family is one of the most common causes of marriage failure. Do you both want children? How many? How will you raise t...

cards.title: The Children Question
cards.text:
This is non-negotiable territory:

If one person wants children and the other does not, there is no compromise.

Someone will be forced to give up something essential.

Questions to align on:

- Do you want children? (Be honest, not hopeful they will change.)
- How many children do you envision?
- When would you want to start trying?
- What if you cannot have biological children? (Adoption? Fertility treatment? Childless?)
- How would you approach unexpected pregnancy?

These conversations should happen before serious commitment, not after engagement.

cards.title: Parenting Philosophy
cards.text:
If you both want children, explore parenting vision:

Discipline approach: How would you handle misbehavior? What is your view on discipline?

Education: Public school, private school, homeschool? How important is this?

Faith formation: How would you raise children spiritually?

Work and parenting: Will one parent stay home? Both work? How will you handle childcare?

Extracurriculars: Heavily scheduled or more free time?

Technology: What boundaries would you set?

You will not agree on everything, but you need to be in the same general direction and able to work through differences.

cards.title: Values Under Pressure
cards.text:
Think about a moment of stress, conflict, or disappointment in a past relationship.

How did each of you respond when things did not go your way?

Write a few lines about what that moment revealed about values such as honesty, humility, responsibility, or empathy.

These patterns often matter more than shared interests.

cards.title: Extended Family Dynamics
cards.text:
Family compatibility extends beyond your household:

Involvement level: How involved will parents and in-laws be? Are expectations aligned?

Boundaries: Can you both set healthy boundaries with family? Or will family interference be a constant battle?

Holidays: How will you navigate competing family expectations?

Geography: Do either of you feel obligated to live near family? Would moving away cause major conflict?

Family dysfunction: If there are unhealthy family patterns, are they acknowledged? Are boundaries in place?

You marry into a family system, not just a person.

Understand what you are entering.

cards.title: Your Family Vision
cards.text: What would you need alignment on before marriage?

cards.title: A Prayer for Family Alignment
cards.text:
Lord, give me wisdom about family and children.

Help me be honest about what I want and need.

Bring me someone whose vision for family aligns with mine.

Prepare us both to build a family that honors You.

Amen.

activities.title: Financial Compatibility: Money and Values
activities.subtitle: Evaluating alignment on finances, spending, and stewardship
activities.whyThisMatters: Money is one of the top sources of conflict in marriage. But the conflict is rarely about money itself; it is about values, security, control, and priorities. Understanding financial compatibility helps you avoid one of the most common marriage struggles.

frameworkBasis.explanation: Money is one of the top sources of conflict in marriage. But the conflict is rarely about money itself; it is about values, security, control, and pri...

cards.title: Money Reveals Values
cards.text:
How someone handles money reveals deeper values:

A spender may value experiences, generosity, or living in the moment.

A saver may value security, planning, or delayed gratification.

A giver may value generosity, faith, or helping others.

A hoarder may value control, fear scarcity, or distrust.

None of these is automatically right or wrong.

But significant misalignment creates constant tension.

The question is not just

"How do they handle money?" but

"What does their money behavior reveal about their values?"

cards.title: Areas to Evaluate
cards.text:
Explore these financial areas:

Current situation: Do they have debt? Savings? What is their financial health?

Spending vs. saving: What is their natural tendency? Is it compatible with yours?

Generosity: What role does giving play? Tithing? Charitable giving?

Lifestyle expectations: What standard of living do they expect? Is it realistic? Compatible with yours?

Career and income: What are their career plans? Are they ambitious? Content? How does this affect finances?

Financial transparency: Are they open about their finances? Or secretive?

Debt philosophy: How do they view debt? Credit cards? Loans?

cards.title: Financial Conversations to Have
cards.text:
Before marriage, discuss:

- What is your current financial situation? (Debt, savings, income)
- What are your financial goals?
- How do you feel about budgeting?
- What role should giving and tithing play?
- How do you view debt?
- What lifestyle do you expect or hope for?
- How should finances be managed in marriage? (Joint accounts? Separate? Both?)
- What was money like in your family growing up?
- What are your biggest financial fears?

These conversations should happen before engagement, not after.

cards.title: Your Financial Values
cards.text: What would financial compatibility look like for you?

cards.title: A Prayer for Financial Wisdom
cards.text:
Lord, help me steward money wisely and find a partner who shares this commitment.

Reveal any unhealthy patterns in my own finances.

Bring me someone with whom I can build financial partnership that honors You.

Amen.

activities.title: Life Vision: Heading the Same Direction
activities.subtitle: Evaluating alignment on where your lives are going
activities.whyThisMatters: You can love someone deeply and still be heading different directions. Career ambitions, geographic preferences, lifestyle choices, and life goals all matter. If your visions do not align, you will spend marriage pulling against each other.

frameworkBasis.explanation: You can love someone deeply and still be heading different directions. Career ambitions, geographic preferences, lifestyle choices, and life goals all...

cards.title: Vision Alignment Matters
cards.text:
Imagine two scenarios:

Couple A: She wants to climb the corporate ladder and live in a major city. He wants a simple life in a small town with lots of family time.

Couple B: Both want meaningful careers with flexibility.

Both value community over status.

Both are open to adventure but prioritize stability.

Couple A will spend their marriage in conflict over every major decision.

Couple B will navigate decisions as a team heading the same direction.

You need to know: Where is this person's life heading? Is it compatible with where my life is heading?

cards.title: Areas of Life Vision
cards.text:
Explore alignment in these areas:

Career: How ambitious are they? What role should work play? Would they relocate for a job?

Geography: Where do they want to live? City, suburbs, rural? Near family or independent?

Lifestyle: Fast-paced or relaxed? Social or quiet? Adventurous or stable?

Purpose: What do they want their life to be about? What impact do they want to make?

Retirement: What do they envision for later life?

Ministry and service: What role should serving others play?

You do not need identical visions, but you need compatible ones.

cards.title: Vision Questions to Explore
cards.text:
Ask each other:

- Where do you see yourself in 5, 10, 20 years?
- What do you want your life to be about?
- How important is career advancement to you?
- Where would you ideally live? Would you move for opportunity?
- What does a good life look like to you?
- What would you regret not doing?
- How do you want to spend your time and energy?
- What role should ministry or service play?

Listen for alignment or tension in vision.

cards.title: Your Life Vision
cards.text: What would you need to see in a partner's life direction to feel compatible?

cards.title: A Prayer for Shared Direction
cards.text:
Lord, show me where You are leading my life.

Bring me someone heading the same direction, someone I can walk with rather than pull against.

Align both our visions with Yours.

Amen.

activities.title: Communication and Conflict Compatibility
activities.subtitle: Evaluating how you handle disagreement together
activities.whyThisMatters: Every couple disagrees. The question is not whether you will have conflict but how you will handle it. Compatible communication and conflict styles allow resolution and growth. Incompatible styles create repeated damage and accumulating resentment.

frameworkBasis.explanation: Every couple disagrees. The question is not whether you will have conflict but how you will handle it. Compatible communication and conflict styles al...

cards.title: Why This Compatibility Matters
cards.text:
Research by John Gottman shows that how couples handle conflict predicts marriage success more than the amount of conflict they have.

Compatible conflict styles:
- Both can express concerns without attacking
- Both can listen without becoming defensive
- Both take responsibility for their part
- Both can restore after conflict
- Conflict leads to understanding, not damage

Incompatible conflict styles:
- One pursues while the other withdraws
- One attacks while the other shuts down
- Neither takes responsibility
- Conflict escalates rather than resolves
- Damage accumulates over time

cards.title: What to Observe
cards.text:
Watch how they handle disagreement:

• Do they attack your character or address the issue?

• Do they give the silent treatment or engage?

• Do they hold grudges or move forward?

• Do they fight to win or fight to understand?

• You will see their conflict style during dating.

• Believe what you see.

cards.title: Your Communication Style
cards.text: What style in a partner would be compatible with yours?

cards.title: Conflict Compatibility Check
cards.text:
Ask yourselves:

- Have we navigated a real disagreement? How did it go?
- Did we both feel heard?
- Did we resolve it or just drop it?
- Were we able to restore and reconnect?
- Did either of us attack, stonewall, or become contemptuous?
- Do I feel safe bringing up concerns with this person?

If you have not had significant conflict yet, you do not know this compatibility. Do not commit until you do.

cards.title: A Prayer for Healthy Communication
cards.text:
Lord, help me be a healthy communicator.

Change my own patterns where they need to change.

Bring me someone with whom I can work through conflict without destroying connection.

Teach us both Your way of handling disagreement.

Amen.

activities.title: Emotional and Relational Needs
activities.subtitle: Understanding how you each need to give and receive love
activities.whyThisMatters: People have different emotional needs and different ways of expressing love. What makes one person feel loved might not register with another. Understanding these differences and evaluating compatibility prevents the frustration of loving someone in ways they do not receive.

frameworkBasis.explanation: People have different emotional needs and different ways of expressing love. What makes one person feel loved might not register with another. Underst...

cards.title: Love Languages
cards.text:
Gary Chapman's love languages framework describes five ways people express and receive love:

Words of

Affirmation: Verbal expressions of love, appreciation, and encouragement.

Quality

Time: Focused, undivided attention and presence.

Acts of

Service: Doing helpful things that make life easier.

Physical

Touch: Appropriate physical affection and closeness.

Gifts: Thoughtful presents that show you were thinking of them.

Most people have one or two primary languages.

Speaking your partner's language makes them feel loved; speaking only your own may leave them feeling unloved despite your efforts.

cards.title: Compatibility in Emotional Needs
cards.text:
Consider these aspects:

Affection needs: How much physical affection do you each need? Is there a significant gap?

Time needs: How much togetherness versus independence do you each need?

Validation needs: How much reassurance and affirmation do you each require?

Intimacy pace: How quickly do you each open up emotionally?

Support style: When stressed, do you want space or closeness? Advice or listening?

Significant gaps in emotional needs can create chronic dissatisfaction, where one person always wants more than the other can give.

cards.title: Exploring Emotional Needs
cards.text:
Discuss together:

- What makes you feel most loved?
- What is your love language? What is mine?
- How much alone time versus together time do you need?
- When you are stressed, what do you need from a partner?
- What would make you feel neglected?
- How do you express love naturally?

Also observe: Are they willing to learn your language? Or do they only express love their way?

cards.title: Your Emotional Needs
cards.text: What emotional needs would you struggle to meet in a partner?

cards.title: A Prayer for Emotional Connection
cards.text:
Lord, help me understand my own needs and learn to meet the needs of another.

Bring me someone with whom I can build deep emotional connection, where we both feel loved and valued.

Teach me to love well.

Amen.

activities.title: Roles and Expectations in Marriage
activities.subtitle: Aligning on how you will function as a team
activities.whyThisMatters: Unspoken expectations about roles in marriage cause tremendous conflict. Who handles what? Who leads in what areas? What does partnership look like? These assumptions need to become explicit conversations before marriage.

frameworkBasis.explanation: Unspoken expectations about roles in marriage cause tremendous conflict. Who handles what? Who leads in what areas? What does partnership look like? T...

cards.title: The Expectation Problem
cards.text:
Everyone enters marriage with expectations, often unexamined:

- He assumes she will handle the household like his mother did.
- She assumes he will be emotionally available like her father was not.
- He expects her to manage the social calendar.
- She expects him to handle all finances.

When expectations are unspoken, they become disappointments.

When they are spoken, they become negotiations.

The goal is not identical expectations but awareness of differences and willingness to work through them.

cards.title: Areas to Discuss
cards.text:
Discuss expectations in these areas:

Household: Who handles cooking, cleaning, maintenance, organization?

Finances: Who manages money, pays bills, makes financial decisions?

Decisions: How are major decisions made? Who has final say?

Career: Whose career takes priority? How will you handle conflicts?

Social life: Who maintains friendships and plans social activities?

Emotional labor: Who tracks birthdays, appointments, family needs?

Spiritual leadership: What does this look like in your marriage?

Childcare: If children come, how will responsibilities divide?

cards.title: Expectations Conversation
cards.text:
Have this conversation:

• "What do you expect marriage to look like day-to-day?"

• "How did your parents divide responsibilities?"

• "What household tasks do you expect to handle? Expect your spouse to handle?"

• "How do you think decisions should be made?"

• "What does headship and submission mean to you practically?"

• "Where do you think we might have different expectations?"

• Listen without judgment.

• Seek understanding before agreement.

cards.title: Your Role Expectations
cards.text: Where might you have unconscious assumptions?

cards.title: A Prayer for Partnership
cards.text:
Lord, help me see my own expectations clearly.

Prepare me to be a true partner, not someone demanding my way.

Bring me someone with whom I can build a marriage of mutual service and love.

Align our expectations with Your design.

Amen.

activities.title: When You Do Not Align: Handling Differences
activities.subtitle: Distinguishing workable differences from fundamental incompatibility
activities.whyThisMatters: No two people align perfectly. The question is not whether you have differences but whether your differences are workable. Some differences enrich a marriage; others destroy it. Learning to distinguish between them helps you make wise decisions.

frameworkBasis.explanation: No two people align perfectly. The question is not whether you have differences but whether your differences are workable. Some differences enrich a m...

cards.title: Types of Differences
cards.text:
Enriching differences:
- One is spontaneous, one is organized (balance)
- One is introverted, one is extroverted (stretching)
- Different strengths that complement each other

Workable differences:
- Different preferences that can be negotiated
- Different backgrounds that require understanding
- Different opinions on non-essential matters

Fundamental incompatibilities:
- Different on core values (faith, family, integrity)
- Different life directions with no overlap
- Different on non-negotiables (children, major life choices)
- Character issues that will not change

The first two types can strengthen a marriage.

The third type predicts failure.

cards.title: Questions for Evaluation
cards.text:
For any difference, ask:

Is this a core value or a preference? Core values are non-negotiable; preferences are flexible.

Is this changeable? Some things can grow; others are fixed.

Can we both live with the difference long-term? Not just tolerate it, but genuinely accept it?

Does this difference create richness or resentment? Some differences complement; others clash.

Would I be trying to change them? If you are hoping they will become different, that is a warning sign.

Have we discussed it openly? Hidden differences become bigger over time.

cards.title: Difference Assessment
cards.text:
For each significant difference you have identified:

1. Name the difference clearly.
2. Categorize it: enriching, workable, or fundamental?
3. Discuss it openly with your partner.
4. Determine: Can you both genuinely live with this?
5. Be honest: Are you hoping they will change?

If you have fundamental incompatibilities on core issues, no amount of love will overcome them. Be honest now rather than divorced later.

cards.title: Your Differences Evaluation
cards.text:
If you are in a relationship, what differences exist? Are they enriching, workable, or fundamental?

If single, what differences could you accept? What differences are deal-breakers?

cards.title: A Prayer for Wisdom
cards.text:
Lord, give me wisdom to know the difference between workable differences and fundamental incompatibility.

Help me accept what can be accepted and recognize what cannot. Do not let me marry hoping for change that will not come.

Amen.

activities.title: Having the Hard Conversations
activities.subtitle: Practical guidance for discussing difficult topics
activities.whyThisMatters: Many couples avoid hard conversations, hoping issues will resolve themselves. They do not. The conversations you avoid before marriage become the conflicts that damage your marriage. Learning to have these conversations with skill sets you up for success.

frameworkBasis.explanation: Many couples avoid hard conversations, hoping issues will resolve themselves. They do not. The conversations you avoid before marriage become the conf...

cards.title: Why We Avoid Hard Topics
cards.text:
People avoid difficult conversations because:

- Fear of conflict or their reaction
- Fear of what the answers might reveal
- Hope that it will work out without discussion
- Not knowing how to bring it up
- Wanting to preserve the "honeymoon" feeling

But avoidance has a cost.

Unaddressed issues do not disappear; they grow.

And discovering incompatibility after marriage is far more painful than discovering it before.

cards.title: How to Have Hard Conversations
cards.text:
A framework for difficult discussions:

1. Choose the right time.

Not when tired, stressed, or distracted.

2. Set the context. "I want to talk about something important because I care about our future."

3. Be curious, not interrogating.

Ask open questions.

Seek to understand.

4. Share your own position honestly. Do not hide what you really think or want.

5. Listen without judgment.

Let them share fully before responding.

6. Acknowledge differences. Do not pretend you agree when you do not.

7. Discuss implications.

"What does this mean for us?"

8. Decide together.

Can you both live with this? What needs to change?

cards.title: Topics That Must Be Discussed
cards.text:
Before engagement, you should have discussed:

- Faith and spiritual expectations
- Children (whether, when, how many, how to raise)
- Finances (debt, spending, saving, giving)
- Career and ambitions
- Where to live
- Family involvement and boundaries
- Past relationships and history
- Sexual expectations
- Roles and responsibilities
- Conflict handling
- Deal-breakers and non-negotiables

If you cannot discuss these topics, you are not ready to marry.

cards.title: Your Conversation Inventory
cards.text:
Which hard conversations have you had? Which are you avoiding?

What is keeping you from having the conversations you need to have?

cards.title: A Prayer for Courage
cards.text:
Lord, give me courage to have the conversations I have been avoiding.

Help me seek truth even when it is uncomfortable.

Help me speak honestly and listen well.

I trust You with whatever we discover.

Amen.

activities.title: Your Compatibility Assessment
activities.subtitle: Bringing everything together into clear evaluation
activities.whyThisMatters: You have explored many areas of compatibility. Now it is time to consolidate what you have learned into a clear framework for evaluating any relationship you enter.

frameworkBasis.explanation: You have explored many areas of compatibility. Now it is time to consolidate what you have learned into a clear framework for evaluating any relations...

cards.title: What You Can Now Evaluate
cards.text:
You now have frameworks for assessing:

- Chemistry versus compatibility (both matter)
- Core values and non-negotiables (yours and theirs)
- Faith compatibility (foundation for everything)
- Family and children vision (alignment required)
- Financial values (reveals deeper priorities)
- Life vision and direction (heading together or apart)
- Communication and conflict styles (predicts success)
- Emotional needs (how you give and receive love)
- Role expectations (spoken, not assumed)
- Workable versus fundamental differences

This is comprehensive evaluation for marriage readiness.

cards.title: Your Compatibility Checklist
cards.text:
For any serious relationship, evaluate:

• __ Faith: Are we aligned spiritually?
• __ Family: Do we share vision for children and family?
• __ Finances: Are our money values compatible?
• __ Direction: Are we heading the same way?
• __ Communication: Can we navigate conflict well?
• __ Emotional: Do we understand each other's needs?
• __ Expectations: Have we discussed roles openly?
• __ Differences: Are remaining differences workable?
• __ Conversations: Have we discussed the hard topics?
__ Character: Is their character worthy of lifelong commitment?

Green across all areas suggests readiness.

Red in any area requires serious attention.

cards.title: Your Compatibility Summary
cards.text:
If you are in a relationship, how does it score on these areas? Where are you strong? Where are there concerns?

If single, what are your requirements for compatibility in your next relationship?

cards.title: Compatibility Is Discoverable
cards.text:
Here is the good news: compatibility is not a mystery. It is discoverable through honest conversation, observation, and time.

You do not have to wonder.

You do not have to hope.

You can actually know whether you are compatible by doing the work of evaluation.

This takes courage. It requires asking hard questions and accepting honest answers.

But the clarity is worth the discomfort.

Better to discover incompatibility now than to live with it for a lifetime.

cards.title: A Prayer for Clear Evaluation
cards.text:
Lord, thank You for the wisdom to evaluate compatibility thoroughly.

Help me use what I have learned.

Give me courage to ask hard questions and accept honest answers.

Guide me to someone with whom I share both chemistry and compatibility. I trust You with my future.

Amen.

cards.title: Your Declaration
cards.text:
Declare this over your dating life:

• "I will evaluate compatibility, not just chemistry.

• I will know my own values and non-negotiables.
• I will assess faith, family, finances, and direction.
• I will observe communication and conflict styles.
• I will discuss expectations openly.
I will distinguish workable differences from fundamental incompatibilities.
I will have the hard conversations.

I deserve both chemistry and compatibility. I will not settle for one without the other.

I will see clearly and choose wisely."
